acceptance: config exposes a resolved writable data root and the resolver honours AUDIOMANCER_DATA_DIR ahead of every other candidate on every platform.

With no override and a writable application root, the resolved data root is the application root, so APP_SETTINGS_PATH and the log directory keep their current locations for source-tree and portable runs.

With no override and a non-writable application root, the resolved data root is %LOCALAPPDATA%/AudioMancer on Windows, XDG_DATA_HOME/AudioMancer or ~/.local/share/AudioMancer on Linux, and ~/Library/Application Support/AudioMancer on macOS.
A writable PyInstaller _MEIPASS extraction directory is never selected as the data root; the per-user location is used instead.
config.APP_SETTINGS_PATH and the application log directory both derive from the resolved data root rather than directly from config.APP_ROOT.
A read-only application root no longer prevents startup: settings load and save plus logging initialization all succeed against the per-user fallback location.
initialize_logging() does not raise when the log directory cannot be created or the log file cannot be opened; it installs a console-only root logger, records that logging degraded, and returns None.
app.main() completes its bootstrap normally when logging initialization produced no log file.

On first run with no settings file at an active settings path that differs from the bundled default path, settings are seeded from the bundled default file when it is readable and valid, and from build_default_settings() otherwise; the bundled file is never written to.
config exposes the bundled default settings path separately from the active settings path.
The frozen-bundle resource contract still resolves prompts, help, licences and version from the bundle root, and settings.json still counts as a runtime-resource marker.
The configured test and lint gates pass, and audit traceability and audit coverage report no blocking findings.
assumptions: Human decision: the resolver is pure stdlib rather than QStandardPaths, because config.py is imported by every module including headless tests and must not pull in PySide6, and QStandardPaths.AppDataLocation appends QCoreApplication applicationName, which is still empty when config is imported during bootstrap.

Human decision: relocation is conditional. A writable application root keeps settings and logs in place, so source-tree, portable-zip and developer runs behave identically to today and the existing contract tests keep asserting the same paths. Only a genuinely non-writable install root falls back to the OS per-user location.

Writability is proven by an actual probe file created and removed under the application root, not by os.access, because on Windows os.access(path, os.W_OK) ignores directory ACLs and reports Program Files as writable.

The PyInstaller _MEIPASS extraction directory must be excluded from the portable branch even though it is writable, otherwise a onefile build would persist settings into a temporary folder that the bootloader deletes on exit.

The app-root settings.json stays committed and packaged as the read-only default scaffold; it keeps working as a runtime-root marker in _has_runtime_resource_markers() and seeds the per-user file when the two paths differ, so an existing installation keeps its settings on first run after the change.

Windows and Linux fallback behaviour is verified by monkeypatched platform and environment tests on the local Windows host; no Linux runner is available in this environment, so cross-platform proof is test-level rather than execution-level.
alignment.reason: Policy alignment.risk_threshold = medium forces decision pause at this risk level, so pause is recorded for audit even though the human already answered all three design questions and explicitly approved the medium risk in chat on 2026-07-25. No open questions remain; the run advances on that recorded human approval.
scope: IN: a writable-data-root resolver in config.py (AUDIOMANCER_DATA_DIR override, then a writable application root for portable and source runs, then the OS per-user data location) plus new constants for the resolved data root, the active settings path and the bundled default settings path; APP_SETTINGS_PATH and the logging directory repointed to the resolved data root; a guard that never treats the PyInstaller _MEIPASS extraction directory as a portable root; initialize_logging() degraded to console-only on OSError instead of raising, with a Path-or-None return; log retention cleanup made tolerant of filesystem errors; settings_service first-run seeding from the bundled default settings file; app.py bootstrap made resilient to a logging init that produced no file; new and updated tests; component documentation; requirement snapshots. OUT: moving read-only packaged resources (prompts, help, LICENSE, icon, pyproject) off APP_ROOT; any change to settings schema, defaults, validation rules or the settings UI; project-workspace paths and per-project artifacts, which are already operator-chosen; the APP_ROOT default directory used by the project open/create file dialogs; log format, retention or level policy; adding PySide6 QStandardPaths as a config.py dependency; packaging and installer changes.
alignment.source: User chat ticket 3: 'settings.json si Logs/ scriu in APP_ROOT - cade pe instalari read-only (Linux SI Windows)', citing config.py:180, logging_service.py:176, app.py:50, action 'muta datele per-user'. Human answers recorded in chat on 2026-07-25: medium risk explicitly approved; resolver is pure stdlib platform plus environment variables, not QStandardPaths; relocation is conditional, keeping data in the application root when that root is writable (portable mode).
alignment.understanding: config.APP_SETTINGS_PATH (config.py:180) and logging_service._log_directory_path() (logging_service.py:176) both derive writable runtime data from config.APP_ROOT, which resolve_app_runtime_root() sets to the source-tree root, the installed wheel resource root, or the PyInstaller bundle root. For a frozen build installed into a non-writable location (Program Files on Windows, a system-wide prefix on Linux), settings.json cannot be written and Logs/ cannot be created. initialize_logging() calls log_directory.mkdir(parents=True) and then logging.FileHandler(...), and app.py:50 calls it before the try/except, so an OSError there aborts startup with a raw traceback and no log file at all. The fix separates two concerns. First, a new writable-data-root resolver decides once, at import time, where per-user data lives: an explicit AUDIOMANCER_DATA_DIR override wins; otherwise the application root is used when it actually accepts writes (preserving portable and source-tree behaviour exactly as today); otherwise the OS per-user data location is used (%LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows, XDG_DATA_HOME or ~/.local/share on Linux, ~/Library/Application Support on macOS). settings.json and the Logs directory both move to that resolved root, and the app-root settings.json becomes the read-only bundled default that seeds the per-user copy on first run. Second, initialize_logging() becomes non-fatal, degrading to a console-only root logger and returning None when the log directory or log file cannot be opened, so an unusable data location can never crash the bootstrap before logging exists. Read-only packaged resources (prompts, help, LICENSE, icon, pyproject) stay under APP_ROOT and are unchanged.

intent.statement: Move per-user writable application data (settings.json and the Logs directory) out of the application root into a per-user OS data location (%LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows, $XDG_DATA_HOME or ~/.local/share on Linux, ~/Library/Application Support on macOS) with an AUDIOMANCER_DATA_DIR override, keep the app-root settings.json as a read-only bundled default that seeds the per-user file on first run, and make initialize_logging degrade to console-only instead of raising so a read-only install directory (Program Files or a system-wide Linux install) can no longer crash startup before any log exists.

spec_items.statement: config.resolve_user_data_root() returns the AUDIOMANCER_DATA_DIR override when set and non-empty, otherwise the application root when a probe file proves it writable and it is not the PyInstaller _MEIPASS extraction directory, otherwise the per-user OS data location (%LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support on macOS, $XDG_DATA_HOME or ~/.local/share elsewhere), each suffixed with the application name.

examples: With AUDIOMANCER_DATA_DIR=D:\AM-data: APP_SETTINGS_PATH=D:\AM-data\settings.json and logs land in D:\AM-data\Logs
spec_items.statement: config.APP_SETTINGS_PATH equals APP_USER_DATA_ROOT / settings.json and the logging service log directory equals APP_USER_DATA_ROOT / APP_LOG_DIRECTORY_NAME; neither is composed from config.APP_ROOT.

examples: Bundled settings.json contains language=ro; first run with an empty per-user data root writes language=ro to the per-user settings file and leaves the bundled file byte-identical
spec_items.statement: settings_service.ensure_settings_file() seeds a missing active settings file from the validated bundled default payload at config.APP_DEFAULT_SETTINGS_PATH when that path differs from the active path and holds a readable JSON object, and from build_default_settings() otherwise; the bundled file is never written.

examples: mkdir raising PermissionError -> initialize_logging() returns None, root logger holds exactly one StreamHandler, and app.main() still returns the QApplication exit code
spec_items.statement: logging_service.initialize_logging() returns Path or None and raises no OSError: on log-directory or log-file failure it installs a console-only root logger, emits one logging-degraded warning naming the path and error, and returns None; _cleanup_old_log_files swallows filesystem errors; app.main() completes its bootstrap when the returned path is None.
